```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>",
  fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4.6, dpi = 110,
  warning = FALSE
)
```

The discard **raising** side of the package again, this time with the groups
defined by the **hierarchical cascade** instead of by hand (vignette **2a**).
It is a walkthrough, not a test: nothing here asserts pass or fail, and it is
the script to run chunk by chunk in RStudio. Vignette **3** compares this
scheme, the manual one and other hierarchies against each other.

RDBESStockCoord has no notion of "cascade from fine to coarse until coverage
clears a bar" - that is rcef's own `recommend_raising()`: a cascade of pools
coarsening from the stratum's own data outward. With enough of its *own*
sampling a stratum is not pooled at all; otherwise it is pooled with strata
sharing less and less of the hierarchy, in the order given, each level with
its own coverage threshold. `conds_from_auto()` is the minimal glue turning
that recommendation into the same `strataCond` / `matchedDataCond` shape as
the manual scheme, so the raising call itself is, again, `catchRaising()`
directly: a named list of quosures per method (`strataCond` = which strata a
group claims, `matchedDataCond` = which data its discard rate is estimated
from), checked, then raised.

The last two sections build the same output data sets as 2a - **CC** and
**CAR / CAS** - for this scheme, following the schema of a real ICES
stock-annex CAR / CAS export. They are built inline, as plain data frames, on
purpose: not wrapped in functions and not written to csv yet.

# Data

Brill, `bll.27.3a47de`, 2025, from the CEF csv file under
`inst/extdata/data_CEF_format` (local to this machine; the file is not in the
repository). Only the catch table is needed for raising.

```{r load, message = FALSE}
library(dplyr)
library(rcef)
library(ggplot2)   # the cascade plot below is a one-off ggplot2 call

cef_dir <- file.path("..", "inst", "extdata", "data_CEF_format")

# blank cells (no discard domain, no trip count ...) read as NA
catch_data <- read.csv(file.path(cef_dir, "bll", "bll_2025_catches_CEF_v17.1.csv"),
                       na.strings = "")
```

`derive_fields()` is what turns raw CEF into strata-ready data: `metier4`,
`mesh` and friends out of `fleetValue`, the ICES area levels out of
`areaValue`, plus `Country` and `Season`.

```{r derive}
catch_data <- derive_fields(x = catch_data)
nrow(catch_data)
```

## The stratum resolution

`dims` is the set of columns that defines a stratum here. "Own stratum" *is*
this set of columns - a stratum finer than this cannot be raised on its own
data, because there is no finer resolution defined. Its columns are the same,
in the same order, as the hierarchy below - not by accident: `stratum_id` is
`paste(dims values, sep = " | ")`, which is order-sensitive. If `dims` and
`hierarchy` named the same columns in two different orders (or `dims` missed
one the hierarchy has), they would build two different `stratum_id` strings
for the same stratum, and every `stratum_id %in% c(...)` condition downstream
would silently match nothing. Keep them in sync whenever either one changes.

```{r dims}
dims <- c("Country", "Season", "mesh", "metier4")
strata0 <- build_strata(catch_data = catch_data, dims = dims)
cat(sprintf("%d strata at %s, %s t landed\n",
            nrow(strata0), paste(dims, collapse = " + "),
            format(round(sum(strata0$landings), 1), big.mark = ",")))
```

`stratum_id`, `coverage`, `discard_rate`, `n_measurements` and `numTrips` are
added onto `catch_data` itself, once, here - not a second table kept
alongside it. The conditions the cascade writes are `stratum_id %in% c(...)`,
written against whichever stratum a row belongs to, so the ids have to be on
the CEF rows.

```{r stratum-metrics}
catch_data <- add_stratum_metrics(data = catch_data, dims = dims)
```

# Hierarchical grouping

`hierarchy` lists the keys to pool over: the **first** key listed is pooled
over soonest, the **last** one is kept longest. Here that reads: own stratum
first; then join countries; then seasons; then mesh; then `metier4` alone;
and finally everything.

`thresholds` is the own-stratum bar *first*, then one per hierarchy level -
`length(hierarchy) + 1` values, not `length(hierarchy)`; a single value (as
here) recycles to that length, so all five read 50%.

`recommend_raising()` takes the catch straight in and builds its own strata
(`build_strata(catch_data = catch_data, dims = dims)`, with `dims` defaulting
to `hierarchy` - the same columns `dims` above already used to stamp
`stratum_id`). Pass an already-built stratum table instead and it is used as
it is.

```{r recommend}
hierarchy  <- c("Country", "Season", "mesh", "metier4")
thresholds <- 50

rec <- recommend_raising(strata = catch_data, hierarchy = hierarchy,
                         thresholds = thresholds)
```

## The cascade, step by step

`decision_tree()` reads the recommendation one cascade step at a time: how
many strata, and how much of the landings, each step settles. The first row
reads the same way as every other: every `dims` column at once, nothing pooled
- so the whole table is one consistent progression from all four kept to none.

```{r tree}
tree <- decision_tree(rec = rec, hierarchy = hierarchy, thresholds = thresholds,
                      cumulative = TRUE)
tree[, c("step", "pool", "threshold", "n_strata", "pct_landings",
         "cum_pct_landings")]
```

The cascade is a strict partition - every stratum leaves it at exactly one
step, and the landings add back to the total:

```{r partition}
chk <- check_partition(rec = rec, tr = tree)
cat(sprintf("partition check: %s strata / %s landings accounted for%s\n",
            if (chk$n_ok) "all" else sprintf("%d of %d", chk$n_steps, chk$n_total),
            if (chk$l_ok) "all" else sprintf("%s of %s t", chk$l_steps, chk$l_total),
            if (chk$unassigned > 0)
              sprintf(" (%d unassigned)", chk$unassigned) else ""))
```

How much of the landings each step actually settles - the same `tree`, drawn
instead of read: the bars are the share *first* solved at that step, the line
the running total once every step up to and including it has applied. Both
columns are already there from `decision_tree(..., cumulative = TRUE)`;
nothing new is computed here, only plotted. No rcef plot function takes a
`decision_tree()` table (its shape is one row per *cascade step*, not one row
per stratum), so this is a small one-off ggplot rather than a reused
function, styled with `app_theme()` to match the rest.

```{r tree-plot, fig.height = 5, fig.alt = "Share of landings resolved at each step of the hierarchical cascade, with the running total"}
tree$step <- factor(tree$step, levels = tree$step)   # cascade order, not alphabetical
ggplot(tree, aes(x = step)) +
  geom_col(aes(y = pct_landings), fill = "#4292C6", width = 0.6) +
  geom_line(aes(y = cum_pct_landings, group = 1), colour = "#D7191C", linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_point(aes(y = cum_pct_landings), colour = "#D7191C", size = 2) +
  geom_text(aes(y = cum_pct_landings, label = paste0(cum_pct_landings, "%")),
            vjust = -0.6, size = 3, colour = "#D7191C") +
  scale_x_discrete(labels = tree$pool) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 105), expand = c(0, 0)) +
  labs(title = "Landings resolved at each step of the hierarchical cascade",
       subtitle = "bars: share first solved at that step - line: running total solved so far",
       x = NULL, y = "% of total landings") +
  app_theme() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 40, hjust = 1))
```

## The groups

`conds_from_auto()` turns the recommendation into the two condition lists and
a table of the groups. Each group is one distinct pool. `strataCond` says which
strata the group raises - a strict partition, every stratum is raised by
exactly one group. `matchedDataCond` says which data its discard rate is
estimated from: the pool's shared key values (`raise_condition`), applied to
*all* the catch. A group's donors are therefore not just the strata it raises:
they are every stratum that shares the pool's values, including strata that
were resolved at a finer level in another group.

```{r conds}
auto_conds <- conds_from_auto(rec = rec)

# the group of every stratum, for the CAR further down - the same lookup
# conds_from_auto() itself already built
rec$group_id <- auto_conds$groups$group_id[match(rec$raise_condition,
                                                 auto_conds$groups$raise_condition)]
nrow(auto_conds$groups)
head(auto_conds$groups, 6)
```

## Condition diagnostics, and the raise

`conds_from_auto()` writes its conditions as `stratum_id %in% c(...)` - the id
already on `catch_data` since `add_stratum_metrics()`. Everything else here is
identical to the manual scheme. The engine prints a "Condition diagnostics"
banner for each condition; it is hidden here.

```{r check-h, results = "hide", message = FALSE}
cond_st_h <- check_group_conditions(catch_data = catch_data,
                                    condition_list = auto_conds$strataCond,
                                    domain = "domainCatchDis",
                                    originType = "WGEstimate",
                                    variableType = "WeightLive",
                                    logFile = NULL, append = TRUE)
cond_md_h <- check_group_conditions(catch_data = catch_data,
                                    condition_list = auto_conds$matchedDataCond,
                                    conditionType = "matched_data",
                                    domain = "domainCatchDis",
                                    originType = "WGEstimate",
                                    variableType = "WeightLive",
                                    logFile = NULL, append = TRUE)
```

```{r check-h-result}
strata_matrix_h <- do.call(cbind, cond_st_h)
cat(sprintf("hierarchical: %d rows in no group, %d rows in more than one (both should be 0)\n",
            sum(rowSums(strata_matrix_h) == 0), sum(rowSums(strata_matrix_h) > 1)))
```

```{r raise-h, results = "hide", message = FALSE}
raised_hier <- catchRaising(catch_data = catch_data,
                            condition_raising_st_list = auto_conds$strataCond,
                            condition_matched_data_list = auto_conds$matchedDataCond,
                            type = "discards",
                            originType = "WGEstimate",
                            variableType = "WeightLive",
                            logFile = file.path(tempdir(), "raising_log.txt"))
```

```{r raise-h-result}
cat(sprintf("hierarchical raising: %d rows (%d imported, %d raised)\n",
            nrow(raised_hier),
            sum(raised_hier$importedOrRaised == "imported"),
            sum(raised_hier$importedOrRaised == "raised")))
```

## A variation: cap the donor discard rate of the catch-all

Same cascade mechanics, with one addition: a stratum whose own discard rate
exceeds 70% may not *donate* to the catch-all - the widest, least targeted
group, the one every stratum lands in only because nothing more specific
worked for it, where a single outlier stratum can otherwise drag the whole
pool's rate with it. Every group resolved at a more specific level (its own
stratum, or any of the pools above) is untouched: an `OTB`-only pool still
draws on every `OTB` discard rate there is, 70% or not - only a stratum that
clears *none* of those and falls all the way to the catch-all has its donor
pool capped once it gets there.

The catch-all is always the group whose `raise_condition` is the literal
string `"TRUE"` (`recommend_raising()`'s own convention for the fallback
step). If a hierarchy / threshold combination ever resolves everything before
the fallback step, there is no such group and nothing to cap - a valid
outcome the code has to handle.

```{r cap}
auto_conds_ex <- auto_conds
fb_gid <- auto_conds_ex$groups$group_id[auto_conds_ex$groups$raise_condition == "TRUE"]

if (length(fb_gid)) {
  old_cond <- auto_conds_ex$matchedDataCond[[fb_gid]]
  new_cond <- quo(!!old_cond & (is.na(discard_rate) | discard_rate <= 0.7))

  # what the cap changes: the catch-all's own aggregate donor ratio, before
  # and after - read straight off the two conditions rather than picked apart
  # from catchRaising()'s output afterwards
  fb_ratio <- function(cond) {
    d <- catch_data %>%
      filter(!!cond, !is.na(domainCatchDis), originType == "WGEstimate",
             variableType == "WeightLive")
    lan <- sum(d$total[d$catchCategory == "Lan"], na.rm = TRUE)
    dis <- sum(d$total[d$catchCategory == "Dis"], na.rm = TRUE)
    data.frame(n_domains = n_distinct(d$domainCatchDis),
               landings_t = round(lan / 1000, 2), discards_t = round(dis / 1000, 2),
               discard_rate = round(dis / (lan + dis), 3))
  }
  cat(sprintf("catch-all group is %s (%d strata)\n", fb_gid,
              auto_conds_ex$groups$n_strata[auto_conds_ex$groups$group_id == fb_gid]))
  rbind(uncapped = fb_ratio(old_cond), `capped at DR <= 0.7` = fb_ratio(new_cond))

  auto_conds_ex$matchedDataCond[[fb_gid]] <- new_cond
} else {
  cat("no stratum reached the catch-all at these thresholds - nothing to cap\n")
}
```

`check_group_conditions()` will now *warn* that the excluded high-rate
strata's own discard estimates are "not matched to any raising stratum". That
is not a bug surfacing, it is the point: those strata's own data no longer
informs anyone's rate, not even their own group's.

```{r raise-cap, results = "hide", message = FALSE}
raised_hier_ex <- catchRaising(catch_data = catch_data,
                               condition_raising_st_list = auto_conds_ex$strataCond,
                               condition_matched_data_list = auto_conds_ex$matchedDataCond,
                               type = "discards",
                               originType = "WGEstimate",
                               variableType = "WeightLive",
                               logFile = file.path(tempdir(), "raising_log.txt"))
```

```{r raise-cap-result}
cat(sprintf("hierarchical, DR-capped catch-all: %d rows (%d imported, %d raised)\n",
            nrow(raised_hier_ex),
            sum(raised_hier_ex$importedOrRaised == "imported"),
            sum(raised_hier_ex$importedOrRaised == "raised")))
```

The rest of this vignette uses the uncapped run, `raised_hier`.

# Overview of the raised weight

Imported against raised, at any aggregation. `plot_raised_composition()` takes
any catch-side column on `x` and an optional `facet`: landings / discards are
always the fill, imported / raised is always the shading, and whatever you put
on `x` or `facet` is the aggregation.

```{r overview-table}
raised_overview_table(raised = raised_hier)
```

```{r overview-metier, fig.alt = "Imported and raised weight by metier"}
plot_raised_composition(raised = raised_hier, x_var = "metier4")
```

By country, faceted by season - a finer aggregation than the group
definitions themselves ever used:

```{r overview-country, fig.height = 6.5, fig.alt = "Imported and raised weight by country, one panel per season"}
plot_raised_composition(raised = raised_hier, x_var = "Country", facet_var = "Season")
```

# Discard rate across the raising groups

Not how much weight moved, but whether the *strata a group draws its rate
from* agree with each other. `plot_discard_rate()` draws one point per stratum
from any table carrying a discard rate; put the raising **group** on `x` and
every point under a group is one of the strata that fed its rate - a group
with points scattered from 2% to 40% is not a group, it is a guess, no matter
how well it covers the stock.

Here the donors of a group are *not* the strata it raises - a stratum raised
from a wide pool often has no discard data of its own. So, exactly as for the
manual scheme in 2a, each group's `matchedDataCond` is filtered straight
against `catch_data`, at the `domainCatchDis` granularity `catchRaising()`
itself estimates a ratio from. Each group's rows are turned into donor strata
by `build_coverage_strata()` and fed to `plot_discard_rate()`. The table's
`rate` is discards / covered landings - the very number the CAS output reports
as `rate` (there per CEF row, here per donor stratum), so what is plotted here
is what ends up in the CAS.

```{r donors}
donor_detail_hier <- bind_rows(lapply(names(auto_conds$matchedDataCond), function(g) {
  donors <- catch_data %>%
    filter(!!auto_conds$matchedDataCond[[g]],
           !is.na(domainCatchDis),
           originType == "WGEstimate",
           variableType == "WeightLive") %>%
    build_coverage_strata(dims = c("domainCatchDis", "metier4"))
  # NULL for a group with no landings / discards among its donors at all
  if (!is.null(donors)) mutate(donors, donor_group = g, .before = 1)
}))
```

The highest-numbered group is the catch-all (`raise_condition` is `"TRUE"`),
whose pool is every stratum there is - the widest and least targeted rate.

```{r donors-plot, fig.width = 9, fig.height = 5.5, fig.alt = "Discard rate of the donor strata behind each raising group, coloured by metier"}
plot_discard_rate(catch = donor_detail_hier, x = "donor_group", colour = "metier4",
                  jitter = TRUE)
```

The groups with the most donor strata behind their rate, and how much those
rates spread:

```{r donors-summary}
donor_detail_hier %>% group_by(donor_group) %>%
  summarise(n = n(),
            mean_rate = round(weighted.mean(rate, w = weightingTotal, na.rm = TRUE), 3),
            sd_rate = round(sd(rate, na.rm = TRUE), 3),
            min_rate = round(min(rate, na.rm = TRUE), 3),
            max_rate = round(max(rate, na.rm = TRUE), 3),
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  arrange(desc(n)) %>%
  head(10)
```

# Output: CC (Catch Combined)

One row per `catchCategory`, the stock-wide raised total: total landings and
total (sampled + raised) discards for the stock, in tonnes. One row per
`catchCategory` actually present in `raised_hier` - nothing below is hardcoded
to just `Lan` and `Dis`.

`car_version`, `car_version_desc` and `car_scheme_name` identify *this*
allocation scheme's run. The manual scheme of 2a carries version 1; a
different scheme carries a different one, so several runs' CC / CAR / CAS
outputs can sit in the same downstream table without being confused for each
other. All three are reused as they are in the next section - keep every use
in sync if any of them changes.

```{r cc}
car_version      <- 2
car_version_desc <- "Hierarchical_Cascade"
car_scheme_name  <- "Hierarchical"

# year / workingGroup / stock come straight off the loaded data, not typed in
# by hand - assumed constant across the whole run (one stock, one year); the
# stopifnot catches it loudly if that is ever not true rather than silently
# picking the first value.
year_val         <- unique(catch_data$year)
workingGroup_val <- unique(catch_data$workingGroup)
stock_val        <- unique(catch_data$stock)
stopifnot(length(year_val) == 1, length(workingGroup_val) == 1,
          length(stock_val) == 1)

cc_out <- raised_hier %>%
  filter(originType == "WGEstimate", variableType == "WeightLive") %>%
  group_by(catchCategory) %>%
  summarise(total = round(sum(total, na.rm = TRUE) / 1000, 3), .groups = "drop") %>%
  transmute(recordType = "CC", version = car_version,
            versionDescription = car_version_desc,
            calendarYear = "Y", year = year_val,
            workingGroup = workingGroup_val, stock = stock_val,
            catchCategory,
            seasonType = NA_character_, seasonValue = NA_character_,
            areaType = NA_character_, areaValue = NA_character_,
            fleetValue = NA_character_,
            variableType = "WeightLive", variableUnit = "t",
            total, variance = NA_real_, numTrips = NA_integer_)
cc_out
```

# Output: CAR and CAS (detailed)

Two tables sharing one allocation-scheme identity (`recordType`, `version`,
`versionDescription` and `catchAllocationSchemeName` line up between them, the
same values the CC section already set) - kept as two separate data frames
for now, per-row CAR and per-donor-stratum CAS.

## CAR: every row `catchRaising()` produced

Each row is tagged with the **group** that raised it. `catchAllocationGroupName`
is filled *only* where a row was actually raised (blank on every imported row -
nothing raised it, so there is nothing to name); `imported` is Y / N, matching
the source RDBESStockCoord convention rather than rcef's own "imported" /
"raised" wording.

The group is looked up by `stratum_id` against `rec`'s own `group_id`: the
cascade is a strict partition, so every stratum belongs to exactly one group.
The engine records the same thing in its own `DrGroup` column, which is checked
against the lookup below, so the tag does not depend on an engine column.

```{r car}
raised_hier <- raised_hier %>%
  mutate(.car_group = rec$group_id[match(stratum_id, rec$stratum_id)])

# the engine's own DrGroup agrees with the lookup on every raised row
with(subset(raised_hier, importedOrRaised == "raised"),
     all(DrGroup == .car_group))

car_out <- raised_hier %>%
  mutate(recordType = "CAR",
         version = car_version,
         versionDescription = car_version_desc,
         catchAllocationSchemeName = car_scheme_name,
         catchAllocationGroupName = if_else(importedOrRaised == "raised",
                                            .car_group, NA_character_),
         imported = if_else(importedOrRaised == "imported", "Y", "N")) %>%
  select(-.car_group, -importedOrRaised) %>%
  select(recordType, version, versionDescription, catchAllocationSchemeName,
         catchAllocationGroupName, imported, everything())

cat(sprintf("CAR: %d rows x %d columns (%d imported, %d raised across %d groups)\n",
            nrow(car_out), ncol(car_out),
            sum(car_out$imported == "Y"), sum(car_out$imported == "N"),
            n_distinct(car_out$catchAllocationGroupName, na.rm = TRUE)))
```

`car_out` carries the scheme identity columns first, then every column of the
raised table. The raised rows first, key columns only:

```{r car-head}
car_out %>%
  arrange(desc(imported == "N"), catchAllocationGroupName) %>%
  select(catchAllocationGroupName, imported, vesselFlagCountry, seasonValue,
         areaValue, fleetValue, catchCategory, total) %>%
  head(10)
```

## CAS: the donor strata behind each group's rate

Only the imported `Dis` rows that satisfy at least one group's
`matchedDataCond` - the ones `catchRaising()` actually pulled a rate from.
Unlike CAR this is **not** a partition of the rows: a stratum that is one
group's own donor can also be a donor to the wider groups above it in the
cascade, so it appears once *per group it feeds*, not once per row.

`weightingTotal` and `rate` are per this stratum, matched on `domainCatchDis`
- the column CEF itself uses to link a `Dis` estimate to its domain:
`weightingTotal` is that domain's own landed weight (kg, same unit as `total` -
unlike the CC table, CAR and CAS stay in the CEF's native kg throughout), and
`rate` is this row's discards over that landed weight (discards / landings,
*not* the raising side's `discard_rate` = discards / (landings + discards) -
the same `rate` `build_coverage_strata()` and `plot_discard_rate()` use,
matching the reference CAR-CAS_detailed.csv, where `rate` is exactly
`total / weightingTotal`, occasionally above 1).

```{r cas}
landings_by_domain <- catch_data %>%
  filter(catchCategory == "Lan", originType == "WGEstimate",
         variableType == "WeightLive", !is.na(domainCatchDis)) %>%
  group_by(domainCatchDis) %>%
  summarise(.landings = sum(total, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

cas_out <- bind_rows(lapply(names(auto_conds$matchedDataCond), function(g)
  catch_data %>%
    filter(!!auto_conds$matchedDataCond[[g]], catchCategory == "Dis",
           !is.na(domainCatchDis), originType == "WGEstimate",
           variableType == "WeightLive") %>%
    mutate(catchAllocationGroupName = g))) %>%
  left_join(landings_by_domain, by = "domainCatchDis") %>%
  mutate(recordType = "CAS",
         version = car_version,
         versionDescription = car_version_desc,
         catchAllocationSchemeName = car_scheme_name,
         imported = "Y",
         weightingCategory = "Lan",
         weightingParameter = "WeightLive",
         averagingMethod = "weighted",
         weightingTotal = round(.landings, 3),
         rate = round(total / .landings, 4)) %>%
  select(-.landings) %>%
  select(recordType, version, versionDescription, catchAllocationSchemeName,
         catchAllocationGroupName, imported, everything())

cat(sprintf("CAS: %d donor rows x %d columns across %d groups (%d distinct strata - some strata donate to more than one group)\n",
            nrow(cas_out), ncol(cas_out), n_distinct(cas_out$catchAllocationGroupName),
            n_distinct(cas_out$domainCatchDis)))
```

The first donor rows, key columns only:

```{r cas-head}
cas_out %>%
  arrange(catchAllocationGroupName) %>%
  select(catchAllocationGroupName, vesselFlagCountry, areaValue, fleetValue,
         domainCatchDis, total, weightingTotal, rate) %>%
  head(10)
```

## Do CAR and CAS describe the same groups?

Every group CAR raised something for should have at least one CAS donor row,
and vice versa - the two tables describing the same groups, not two different
countings. A group *can* legitimately fail this: `catchRaising()` and every
donor filter above are restricted to `originType == "WGEstimate"`, so a group
whose own discard records all carry some *other* `originType` (`"Official"`)
has no `WGEstimate` donor at all - CAS then has no row for it, and its CAR
rows raised on nothing get `total = NaN`, not a real weight. That is a genuine
gap in the **scheme** (this group cannot really be raised as defined), not a
bug in these tables - so it is printed by name below, never just a silent
`FALSE`.

```{r linked}
car_groups <- na.omit(unique(car_out$catchAllocationGroupName))
cas_groups <- unique(cas_out$catchAllocationGroupName)
ok_linked <- setequal(car_groups, cas_groups)
cat(sprintf("every CAR group also appears in CAS, and vice versa: %s\n", ok_linked))
if (!ok_linked) {
  raised_no_donor  <- setdiff(car_groups, cas_groups)
  donor_not_raised <- setdiff(cas_groups, car_groups)
  if (length(raised_no_donor))
    cat(sprintf("  raised in CAR but no CAS donor (raised total is NaN - check originType): %s\n",
                paste(raised_no_donor, collapse = ", ")))
  if (length(donor_not_raised))
    cat(sprintf("  donor in CAS but nothing raised under it in CAR: %s\n",
                paste(donor_not_raised, collapse = ", ")))
}
```

`cc_out`, `car_out` and `cas_out` are plain data frames in this session;
nothing was written to a file.
